correctness.rationale: The carrier consists of all nonempty subsets S of each arbitrary finite or infinite nonempty U, disjointness accessibility and one FIXED singleton truth valuation. Splitting worlds by |U|≤3, singleton, top, co-singleton, and both |S| and |U\S| ≥2 yields eight types A–H, with the exact successor-type table A:∅ B:{B} C:{C,F} D:{D,G,H} E:∅ F:{C} G:{D} H:{D,H}. Matching types across models is a back-and-forth bisimulation, valid even for infinite U; characteristic formulas using η=◇(¬p∧◇¬p) separate all eight by depth3, with lower depth signatures 2,6,7,8. This proves 4,64,128,256 Boolean formula equivalence classes, and four-ground-element optimal model size. Independent direct finite original-frame refinement on U sizes 1..6 returned depth classes 2,6,7,8,8, only supporting the full bisimulation argument.
residual_risks: Fixed atom predicate p(S)⇔|S|=1, full nonempty powerset carrier and disjointness relation are essential.
The finite test n≤6 is not used as a proof for infinite ground sets; type-table back-and-forth proof covers them.

value.rationale: Disjointness is the canonical orthogonality relation on Boolean events, and marking atoms is a natural fixed logical observation. The universal eight-state bisimulation quotient, exact depth-three collapse, strict finite exceptions, 4-element cutoff and linear-time satisfiability are a useful and motivated complete expressivity classification, not mere bisimulation renaming.
residual_risks: No claim for arbitrary atom valuations, all Boolean algebras, compatibility frames, graded modality or induced subframes.
